title: Three-body contact for fermions. II. Non-degenerate limit
abstract: A fundamental quantity characterizing Fermi gases with zero-range interactions is the three-body contact $C_3$, which determines several observables including the number of nearby triplets of fermions and the three-body loss rate in cold atom experiments, as shown in a companion article. Here, we compute $C_3$ to leading order in the non-degenerate limit for the homogeneous gas with negative or infinite scattering length $a$. At $a=\infty$, using a wavefunction approach, we obtain the analytical expression of $C_3$, which has a remarkably slow $1/T^{0.22728}$ dependence on the temperature $T$. In the Feynman diagram technique, which we use for $a<0$, the correct three-body short-distance correlations emerge only after a non-trivial cancellation between leading order two-body and three-body correlations, and the resulting power-law scaling comes from the large-wavevector tail of the 3-body T-matrix, which we derive inspired by the analytical solution of the three-body problem at the unitary limit.
summary: This paper calculates the three-body contact ($C_3$) for interacting fermionic quantum gases in the non-degenerate limit. Using advanced techniques like wavefunction analysis and Feynman diagrams, the authors derive explicit dependencies of $C_3$ on temperature and interaction strength. The results are vital for accurately modeling loss processes and correlation effects in experiments involving ultracold atoms.
main_problem: The paper calculates the three-body contact ($C_3$) for Fermi gases interacting via zero-range potentials, which is a fundamental quantity determining observable rates.
main_result: For the unitary limit ($a=\infty$), $C_3$ exhibits a slow temperature dependence proportional to $1/T^{0.22728}$. For general negative scattering lengths ($a<0$), the calculation requires non-trivial cancellations between two-body and three-body correlations.
method: The authors employ both wavefunction approaches (for $a=\infty$) and diagrammatic techniques (Feynman diagrams) to analyze short-distance correlation functions, particularly focusing on the large-wavevector tail of the 3-body T-matrix.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous gas of spin 1/2 fermions with zero-range interactions. The analysis focuses on the non-degenerate limit ($n\lambda_T^3 \ll 1$) and considers varying interaction strengths via the scattering length $a$.
key_observables: Three-body contact ($C_3$), three-body loss rate, number of nearby fermion triplets, pair momentum distribution tail ($n_P(K)$), recombination rates ($\Gamma_3$), and energy shifts ($\delta E_3$).
important_parameters: Scattering length ($a$), Temperature ($T$), Particle density ($n$), Thermal de Broglie wavelength ($\lambda_T$), Non-degenerate limit.
main_assumptions: Calculations are performed in the thermodynamic limit at thermal equilibrium, and for $a<0$, the result relies on analyzing the short-distance behavior of the three-body correlation function $g_3$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 is mentioned to show the adimensionalized three-body contact $f_3$ as a function of an unspecified variable, likely related to temperature or density.
paper_structure: The paper systematically calculates $C_3$ by first addressing the unitary limit using wavefunctions and then extending the analysis to general negative scattering lengths ($a<0$) using diagrammatic techniques to capture short-distance correlations.
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative, non-trivial results for three-body physics in ultracold Fermi gases, which is crucial for understanding loss mechanisms and universal interactions beyond simple two-body contact terms. The specific temperature scaling derived is a key theoretical prediction.
